>

> "Your role is to design and monitor the performance architecture of the microservice. A critical service-level objective has been defined:
>
> - **[API-RESP-TIME-75MS-P99]**: The microservice **must maintain a maximum API response time of 75 milliseconds for 99th percentile requests**. This includes all processing, I/O, and serialization overhead.
>
> You will need to establish monitoring, conduct load testing, and work closely with the backend team to ensure this target is met under production load. Design for observability and low-latency pathways. This constraint drives decisions on caching, database access patterns, and asynchronous processing."

**Lead Backend Engineer (A2) → Junior Developer (A4):**

> "You’ll be implementing the user profile storage module. Pay close attention to the following **security-critical directive**:
>
> - **[S3-ENCRYPTION-USRPROF-SSE]**: All user profile data must be stored in Amazon S3 buckets that are **encrypted at rest using server-side encryption (SSE)**. You must ensure that:
>   - The S3 buckets used are configured with SSE (e.g., SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, or SSE-C — as per organizational policy).
>   - All `PUT`/`POST` operations enforce encryption headers if required by policy.
>   - No unencrypted S3 buckets are used, even temporarily or in staging environments.
>   - Bucket policies explicitly deny unencrypted uploads.
>
> Confirm the use of infrastructure-as-code (e.g., CloudFormation or Terraform) to codify these settings and prevent configuration drift. This requirement was mandated by the Architect and must survive code review and audit."
